Historical Trends
Winter-season (Sep–May) annual metrics with a Bayesian brms smooth (y ~ s(year), 95% CrI) only — no linear regression. Panels (top→bottom): total snowfall; days with snow on the ground (depth > 0); cumulative ski days (≥ park threshold); peak depth; mean DJFM (Dec–Mar) depth; White Holidays mean depth (Dec 25–Jan 2); first→last day with snow > 10 cm (ribbon). Current incomplete season is shown as a point but excluded from the smooths.




















TipAbout the Mud Model





Trail muddiness is estimated from a weighted composite of the top 9 cm of soil moisture (ERA5-Land reanalysis for history, Open-Meteo model for forecast days).
Scoring: A site-specific scale factor is applied to soil wetness, then a logistic sigmoid converts it to an internal 0–10 mud index (0 = bone dry, 10 = impassable). A precipitation boost applies when rainfall exceeds 5 mm in the prior 24 h. The displayed 1–10 trail condition score inverts the mud index (score = 11 − mud index), so 10 = Great conditions and 1 = Avoid.
Frozen: flagged when the 3-day rolling mean of shallow soil temperature (0–7 cm) drops to or below 0°C; single cold air-temperature spikes alone do not trigger it.
Calibration parameters (midpoint, steepness, precip_boost, soil_moisture_scale) are set per park in data/parks.yml. The model has not been validated against field observations — treat scores as estimates, especially near level boundaries.









NoteAbout Snow & Cumulative Ski Days





Winter stats use the park snow season from data/parks.yml (default Sep–May). A day with snow (Historical Trends) is any day with mean snow depth > 0 cm. A ski day counts toward cumulative ski days when daily mean snow depth is at or above the park threshold (default 10 cm / 4 in, park-configurable). White Holidays = mean depth Dec 25–Jan 2; DJFM = mean depth Dec–Mar. First/last cover days use depth > 10 cm. Condition labels use the Avoid→Great snow-score scale (Good typically needs ~10+ cm). Season labels use the September start year (e.g. 2024–25).
